To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the NH2-terminal domain of the Ii molecule is sufficient for association with class II, inhibition of peptide binding, and visualization of the Ii homotrimers.
the NH2-terminal 96 amino acids of the Ii polypeptide are sufficient for class II association.

the region from residues 104 to 183 is required for Ii chain homotrimer formation and that the region from residue 104 to 163 is essential for Ii chain association with class II and inhibition of peptide binding.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the functional mapping of the lumenal region of the Ii-chain.
the identification of regions in the Ii chain that are important for association with class II, peptide binding, and homotrimer formation.
the functional domains of the Ii protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

(a) the region of the Ii molecule that contains the CLIP peptides (amino acids 81-104) is not sufficient for association with class II, but is sufficient to inhibit peptide binding; (b) the NH2-terminal 96 amino acids are required for association and inhibition of peptide binding; (c) a region between amino acids (163-183) is essential for the formation of Ii chain trimerization; (d) the cytoplasmic domain of
the Ii chain contains three distinct regions that are required for its association with class II, for inhibition of peptide binding, and for trimerization, respectively.

(i) the region from amino acids 96 to 104 of the lumenal Ii chain domain is sufficient for class II association; (ii) this region is also sufficient for inhibition of peptide binding; (iii) the region between amino acids (aa) 163 and 182 is essential for homotrimers formation of the Ii lumenal domain.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the region between amino acids (aa) 1- 104 is required for association and peptide binding inhibition, whereas the region between aa 105- 163 is required for trimer formation.
the region from amino acids 81 to 183 is required for the formation of Ii chain trimers, whereas the region from amino acid 104 to 163 is required for association with class II HLA molecules.
the NH2-terminal 104 amino acids of the Ii molecule contain the minimal information for the association of the invariant chain with class II molecules and for the inhibition of peptide binding.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the Ii chain can be functionally divided into three distinct domains: a region that is required for association with class II and inhibition of peptide binding, a region required for trimerization, and a region required for targeting of class II-Ii complexes.
Ii chain homotrimerization is an essential feature for the association with class II.
the region between amino acids (aa) 163 and 193 of Ii chain is essential for visualization of homotrimers.
